- 34 -

Sacred Dance Guild 20th Anniversary Festival

Endicott College Beverly, Mass.

June 21-25, 1978

The Variety and The Unity of Spiritual Gifts....I Corinthians 12:4-7

"There is a variety of gifts but always the same Spirit; there are all sorts of service to be done, but always to the same Lord; working in all sorts of different ways in different people, it is the same God who is working in all of them......"

Through the years the Sacred Dance Guild has offered leadership in a variety of dance forms and religious denominations and with this 20th anniversary year we continue to build on the foundation of both traditional and contemporary expression. With this and in coming Festivals the culmination of the conference will be in the creating, participation and experience of a particular denominational worship service and its time in history.

Artists In Leadership

Dance

The Spirit Moves - A Workshop In Dance and Prayer - Through the interaction of self, improvisation and prayer the workshop will explore a variety of ways dance and prayer can enhance liturgy and illuminate scripture varying with the feasts and seasons in the church year allowing us to become more involved in the word of God as it touches us.

Carla DeSola, a graduate of the Juilliard School of Music, has danced and given workshops on dance and prayer from California to New York, for colleges, retreat centers, parishes and religious conferences. She has produced for television, writes a monthly column on dance for Liturgy and is the author of Learning Through Dance and The Spirit Moves .... a handbook on dance and prayer. Presently she is teaching at the College of New Rochelle, New York Theological Seminary and directing the Omega Liturgical Dance Company of New York City.

Music

Calliope Consort - Music for Worship and Dance - Music from biblical times through the 17th century will be played on medieval, renaissance, baroque and folk instruments such as violas da gamba, recorders, krummhorns, pipe and tabor, percussion, harp, rauschefeiffe, psaltry and cornamuse.

The Calliope Consort is directed by Nancy Nichols and assisted by Sybille Volz and members of the Consort. The group has performed at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston; The Fogg Museum, Cambridge; the chapel at the Mass. General Hospital; before the Middlesex Health Association; at lecture demonstrations and for many schools and libraries. In addition to numerous church services, worship and wedding celebrations of a variety of denominations, they have participated in Shakespear's Twelfth Night as well as their own original creation.
